visas.title: General Work Visa
visas.intro: For foreign nationals with a qualifying offer of employment where the prescribed labour-market and employer requirements are met.
visas.qualifies: Applicants with a compliant South African job offer and employer support who satisfy the general work visa requirements.
documents: Signed employment contract and employer undertaking
Department of Employment and Labour certification, where required
SAQA evaluation of foreign qualifications
Proof of relevant experience and professional registration

visas.title: Critical Skills Work Visa
visas.intro: For professionals whose occupation and credentials align with South Africa’s published critical skills framework.
visas.qualifies: Applicants able to demonstrate a listed critical skill, relevant qualifications and any required professional-body registration.
documents: Proof that the occupation appears on the critical skills list
SAQA evaluation and qualification certificates
Professional body registration or confirmation
Employment evidence or proof of active job search, as applicable

visas.title: Business Visa
visas.intro: For qualifying foreign entrepreneurs establishing, investing in or operating a business in South Africa.
visas.qualifies: Applicants meeting the prescribed investment, business viability and employment criteria, subject to any approved reduction or waiver.
documents: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition recommendation
Proof of prescribed available investment funds
Business plan and company registration records
Undertaking regarding South African citizen or permanent-resident employees

visas.title: Visitor’s Visa
visas.intro: For a temporary visit to South Africa for an approved purpose within the conditions of visitor status.
visas.qualifies: Visitors who can show a genuine temporary purpose, sufficient funds, accommodation and an intention to depart.
documents: Proof of purpose and proposed itinerary
Proof of accommodation or host invitation
Recent bank statements or financial support
Return or onward travel arrangements

visas.title: Visitor’s Visa Extension
visas.intro: For eligible visitors seeking authority to remain beyond the period initially granted.
visas.qualifies: Current visitor-visa holders who apply before expiry and can demonstrate a lawful, credible reason for the requested extension.
documents: Current visa and entry stamp
Written motivation for the extension
Proof of continued accommodation and funds
Travel booking or revised departure plan

visas.title: Exchange Visa
visas.intro: For participants in qualifying cultural, economic or social exchange programmes.
visas.qualifies: Applicants accepted into a recognised exchange programme and supported by the relevant programme or institution.
documents: Official exchange programme acceptance
Undertakings from the host or sponsoring institution
Proof of accommodation and financial support
Medical and radiological reports, where prescribed

visas.title: Study Visa
visas.intro: For international students accepted by a registered South African learning institution.
visas.qualifies: Learners accepted for full-time study who can show funding, suitable accommodation and compliant medical cover.
documents: Acceptance letter from a registered institution
Proof of funds for tuition and living costs
South African medical cover or prescribed proof
Accommodation details and guardian consent for minors

visas.title: Medical Treatment Visa
visas.intro: For foreign nationals receiving planned medical treatment in South Africa.
visas.qualifies: Patients with a confirmed treatment plan from a South African medical practitioner or institution and sufficient funding.
documents: Letter from the treating medical practitioner or institution
Treatment plan and estimated duration
Proof of funds for treatment and living costs
Details of an accompanying person, where relevant

visas.title: Crew Visa
visas.intro: For eligible members of transport crews entering or remaining in South Africa for their duties.
visas.qualifies: Crew members supported by a qualifying operator and able to demonstrate their role, route and intended period in South Africa.
documents: Employer or operator confirmation
Crew identification and employment records
Travel route and vessel or aircraft details
Proof of accommodation where required

visas.title: Spousal / Life Partner Visa
visas.intro: For the spouse or qualifying life partner of a South African citizen or permanent resident.
visas.qualifies: Spouses and qualifying life partners able to prove a genuine relationship and the South African partner’s status.
documents: Marriage certificate or evidence of a permanent life partnership
South African ID or permanent residence proof of partner
Notarial agreement and relationship evidence, where applicable
Proof of shared residence and financial support

visas.title: Relative’s Visa
visas.intro: For qualifying immediate family members of South African citizens or permanent residents.
visas.qualifies: Applicants within the prescribed degree of kinship who have eligible South African family support.
documents: Unabridged birth or marriage certificates proving relationship
South African ID or permanent residence proof of relative
Financial assurance from the sponsoring relative
Police clearances where prescribed

visas.title: Retired Person Visa
visas.intro: For applicants who meet the prescribed lifetime income or net-worth threshold for retirement in South Africa.
visas.qualifies: Applicants able to demonstrate the required pension, retirement income or qualifying financial resources.
documents: Proof of pension or irrevocable annuity
Bank statements and evidence of qualifying net worth
Medical and radiological reports
Police clearance certificates from relevant countries

visas.title: Treaty Visa
visas.intro: For activities conducted in South Africa under an applicable international agreement.
visas.qualifies: Applicants whose intended activities fall within a recognised treaty or international agreement involving South Africa.
documents: Confirmation of the applicable treaty or agreement
Official nomination or assignment letter
Details of intended activities and duration
Proof of accommodation and financial support

visas.title: Permanent Residence — Worker
visas.intro: For qualifying workers seeking permanent residence through an eligible employment-based pathway.
visas.qualifies: Applicants who meet the statutory work, residence and employment conditions for direct permanent residence.
documents: Current work visa and complete passport history
Long-term employment contract and employer letter
Proof of qualifying period of lawful employment
SAQA evaluation, qualifications and professional registration

visas.title: Permanent Residence — Spouse / Dependant
visas.intro: For qualifying spouses and dependants seeking permanent residence through a South African citizen or permanent resident.
visas.qualifies: Applicants who meet the prescribed relationship, duration and dependency requirements.
documents: Civil-status certificates proving the relationship
South African ID or permanent residence proof of sponsor
Evidence of qualifying relationship duration
Financial support and dependency evidence, where applicable

visas.title: Visa Waiver / Exemption
visas.intro: For applicants seeking relief from a prescribed visa requirement where a properly motivated case can be made.
visas.qualifies: Applicants with exceptional circumstances and a well-supported legal and factual basis for the requested waiver or exemption.
documents: Detailed legal and factual motivation
Evidence supporting exceptional circumstances
Copy of current or proposed visa application
Relevant employer, family or institutional supporting records

visas.title: Permanent Residence Waiver / Exemption
visas.intro: For permanent residence matters requiring formal relief from a prescribed requirement.
visas.qualifies: Applicants able to establish a lawful basis and compelling circumstances for permanent-residence relief.
documents: Comprehensive waiver or exemption motivation
Permanent residence application context and status records
Evidence of hardship or exceptional circumstances
Supporting affidavits and relevant official correspondence

commonDocuments: Valid passport with sufficient blank pages
Proof of current lawful status and residential address
Police clearances, medical and radiological reports where prescribed

faqs.q: When should I start my immigration application?
faqs.a: Starting early creates time to assess your options and prepare supporting evidence without unnecessary pressure. For most categories we suggest beginning three to six months before you need to travel or before your current status expires.

faqs.q: Can GlobalPath guarantee that my visa will be approved?
faqs.a: No professional consultant can guarantee a government decision. We offer careful guidance and application support based on current requirements, and we tell you plainly where a case has weaknesses.

faqs.q: What happens during an initial consultation?
faqs.a: We discuss your goals, history and circumstances, identify possible routes and outline practical next steps. You receive a written summary afterwards.

faqs.q: Do you work with clients outside South Africa?
faqs.a: Yes. Consultations can be held by video call, and documents can be shared securely through the client portal. Some applications must be submitted at a South African mission abroad; we prepare you for that submission.

faqs.q: What if my application is rejected?
faqs.a: You can usually appeal within a prescribed time limit, so contact us as soon as you receive the outcome. We prepare and lodge appeals for a fixed fee of R5,000.

faqs.q: How are your professional fees structured?
faqs.a: Our professional fee is a fixed R10,000 per application and R5,000 per appeal. Government (DHA) fees and the VFS service fee of R1,790 are separate and are paid at submission.

articles.title: Preparing for a South African immigration application
articles.summary: A practical guide to building an organised evidence file, planning realistic timelines and avoiding common application issues.

body.p: Most delays begin before an application is lodged, when an applicant chooses a category that does not fit their circumstances. Write down why you are coming, for how long, and who is supporting your stay. Those three answers narrow the options considerably, and they are the first things an adjudicator will look for in your file.

Some documents take weeks to obtain: police clearance certificates from every country you have lived in for a year or more, SAQA evaluations of foreign qualifications, and medical and radiological reports. Request these first. Keep a single checklist and record the date each item was issued, because several documents are only accepted if they are recent.

Documents not in English generally need a sworn translation. Copies usually need to be certified. Check the specific requirement for each document before you submit, rather than certifying everything by default.

The Department of Home Affairs publishes target processing times for each category. Treat these as targets rather than promises, and leave a margin before travel dates, contract start dates or the expiry of your current visa.
Retain a complete copy of the submitted application, your VFS receipt and any correspondence. If you need to follow up, appeal or renew, that record is the starting point.

articles.title: Understanding South Africa’s key work visa categories
articles.summary: How the general work, critical skills and intra-company transfer routes differ, and which evidence each one relies on.

body.p: The general work visa is tied to a specific job offer. The employer usually needs to show that the position could not reasonably be filled locally, and the applicant needs qualifications and experience that match the role.

The critical skills route is designed for occupations on the published critical skills list. The emphasis shifts from the employer to the applicant: qualifications, professional registration and experience in the listed occupation carry most of the weight.

Multinational groups can transfer existing employees to a South African branch or affiliate for a limited period. The applicant must already be employed by the group, and the assignment has a defined duration.

Many professionals could qualify under more than one route. The right choice depends on your occupation, how long you plan to stay, whether you may change employers, and whether you intend to apply for permanent residence later.

articles.title: Five immigration considerations for international employers
articles.summary: What HR and mobility teams should put in place before relocating foreign talent to South Africa.

body.h: Map roles to categories before you recruit
body.p: Knowing in advance which visa category a role is likely to fall under helps you set realistic start dates and avoid offers that cannot be supported.
Employers are expected to employ only foreign nationals with valid status that permits the work being done. Maintain copies of each employee's visa and diarise expiry dates well ahead of time.
Spouses and children often need their own applications. Coordinating these with the principal application avoids families arriving on different timelines.

body.h: Budget for timelines, not just fees
body.p: Government fees are modest compared with the cost of a delayed start. Build processing margins into project plans and relocation budgets.
Regulations, critical skills lists and administrative practice change. An annual review of your mobility programme keeps policies and records aligned with current requirements.

articles.title: Planning a family-based immigration application
articles.summary: Spousal, life-partner and relative routes: the relationship evidence that matters and how to present it.

body.p: Family routes depend on showing that the relationship is genuine and continuing. Marriage or birth certificates are the foundation; for life partnerships, evidence of a shared household and financial interdependence carries significant weight.
The South African citizen or permanent resident usually provides undertakings and proof of their own status. Their documents need to be as complete as the applicant's.
Applications involving minors typically require unabridged birth certificates and, where a parent is not travelling, formal consent. Start these early, especially where the other parent lives abroad.
Some family-based temporary visas can lead to permanent residence after a qualifying period. Keeping consistent records from the start makes that later application far simpler.
